title: EU AI Act Article 10 -- Data Governance and Training-Data Provenance
context: 2026-08-14 engine cycle -- EU AI Act Article 10 data-governance duties for high-risk providers are live as of August 2026; training-data provenance is now a verifiable compliance surface, not a data-sheet exercise
body: Article 10 of the EU AI Act turns training data from an engineering detail into a legal requirement. Providers of high-risk AI systems must ensure that the datasets used to train, validate, and test those systems meet stated quality criteria: relevant, sufficiently representative, as free of errors as possible, and complete in view of the intended purpose. The Article also requires data-governance and management practices covering data collection, preparation, and the examination of bias. The answer-first takeaway for a verification-minded operator: provenance is a claim until it is measured. Saying a dataset is representative is an assertion; producing a signed, auditable measurement that the governance practices ran, that the bias examination happened, and that the incident and unparsed rates are surfaced beside accuracy is evidence. The Council of AI positions Article 10 as a credential surface rather than a paperwork one. A deployer who can present a verified measurement credential for training-data provenance -- naming what was measured, on which bank, at which timestamp, and signed by a holder of a published key -- satisfies the duty with records an auditor can re-verify offline, rather than with a self-asserted data card. The boundary language matters too: a data-governance program can honestly claim monitored containment of known data risks, not provable isolation from every possible defect in the training distribution.
